roadmap_scope: Phase 13 is the shared helper tranche, so this lane stays reviewability-only and records the current interop gap between the preexisting list surfaces and the still-missing generic notifier helper surface.

gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 replay now carries a dedicated notifier/list reviewability test so this survey lane stays machine-checkable instead of living only in prose.

A small reviewability gate ties the current list ABI surface, list or hlist view helpers, chrdev-only notifier planning, and the still-missing generic notifier surface together in one repeatable check.
The survey note records the exact current posture on master so later runs do not mistake the chrdev-only notify family for a generic notifier helper or overstate Phase 13 parity.

The current repo already exposes ListHeadRef and HListHeadRef plus the list and hlist summary flags, which means list-shaped interop has a reusable ABI foothold even though it still lives under the Phase 3 helper bundle.
The existing list view helper already models bounded list_head traversal, empty or singular detection, and truncation-aware summaries without claiming list mutation or notifier delivery semantics.
The shared Phase 3 build already replays list_view and hlist_view directly, which makes the current list side of the survey observable on master rather than hypothetical.

Notifier-like behavior in the current repo is still chrdev-local: the notify planner maps chrdev completion state into notify outcomes, but it does not expose a generic notifier_block or notifier_head ABI for shared helper consumers.

The next honest shared-helper step is a tiny generic notifier ABI surface such as notifier_block or notifier_head references that stays read-only and reviewable before any callback registration or chain execution is claimed.

After a generic notifier ABI exists, the smallest follow-up is one bounded helper that only surveys notifier-chain linkage against the existing list_head footprint instead of widening into live registration, priority ordering, SRCU, or blocking-callback behavior.
